label: Barrow
_model: Everything derives from one kernel: an APPETITE and the ACCOMMODATION made for it. The motif, danger, prize kind and faction all follow from the appetite. Cue fragments hang off the MOTIF and are tagged by FACET (institution/ritual/demand/wound/anchor) and level, so two delves sharing a motif draw different imagery. The foreshadow chain is a fixed facet progression mapped onto the arc — which is why area 2's bows and area 4's scratched eyes both point at the same wound.

appeasement.move: look at it and say plainly what you see
appeasement.why: it is being looked at, which is all it ever wanted

appeasement.move: say its name aloud, correctly, unprompted
do one small thing it asks, without arguing
tell it that it has not changed
appeasement.why: it hears that nothing has aged

appeasement.move: admire something of its openly, and mean it
sit down and stay a while

appetites.want: to be told it was not a sin

appeasement.move: tell it that what it did was not a sin
appeasement.why: it is absolved, for a moment

appetites.want: to be first in all things
appetites.purpose: someone would always go behind them

appeasement.move: stand aside and let it go ahead of you

accommodations.text: bound {conscript} by oath they could not break
bought {conscript} from those with nothing left
would not let {conscript} leave, and then could not

looking.dangerLine: the barrow notices those who are seen

institution: mourners carved beside every step, their faces smooth blank ovals
attendants posed facing an empty centre, heads all turned the same way
seats arranged in a half-circle around one chair
ritual: courtiers bent in a bow they have been holding for three hundred years
a receiving line of the dead, still waiting to be presented
gloves laid out for hands that would be kissed
demand: hand-mirrors set into the walls, hundreds, every one angled inward
a chamber where every surface has been polished to show you back
a chair placed so that whoever sits in it must be looked at
wound: portraits of the same woman, the eyes scratched out by fingernails
likenesses turned to face the wall, every one of them
a face chiselled off a statue, and the chisel left behind
anchor: a covered frame the height of a person, facing away from the door
a wardrobe of three hundred dresses in a room with no dust in it
one thing under cloth, and the cloth is clean

naming.dangerLine: to say a name here is to be answered

institution: names cut into the lintel, each one struck through
the dead laid out in the order their names were entered
a register stone, filled edge to edge
ritual: a roll of the dead being read aloud by nobody
grave-goods labelled in a hand that keeps correcting itself
an oath cut into the floor, to be spoken on entering
demand: a wall of tongues in wax, each with a name pressed into it
a chamber that repeats the last name spoken in it
a blank plate at the head of the hall, waiting
wound: a name gouged out so deeply it went through the stone
a ledger with one line scraped away and rewritten forty times
monuments to someone whose name nobody kept
anchor: a book of names with one line left blank
a seal cut with a name worn smooth by rubbing
a tally-stick longer than a person

voices.dangerLine: the dead here still take instruction, and give it

institution: a bell-pull beside every alcove, all of them still taut
servants' bones arranged as though mid-errand
a board of numbered bells, one still swinging
ritual: orders scratched into the floor, the last one unfinished
a speaking-tube running the barrow's length, warm to the touch
a queue of the dead outside a door that never opened
demand: a hall where your own voice arrives before you speak
a seat that expects to be addressed
a room that will not carry sound away from its centre
wound: jaws wired shut, every one of them
an instruction repeated until the stone gave out
a tongue-shaped hollow worn into a step
anchor: a signet still warm, sized for a thumb
a staff of office propped where it was set down
a key that fits nothing here

keeping.dangerLine: nothing here is allowed to change, including you

institution: flowers on the steps that have not wilted or dried
a bed made fresh this morning, three centuries running
lamps trimmed and filled, all of them
ritual: a meal laid out, still warm, for people long past eating
clothes brushed and hung in the order they would be worn
a clock wound by somebody, recently
demand: jars along the wall, each holding a single year
a mirror that shows the room a little younger than it is
a room that resets itself if you look away
wound: a child's shoes, unworn, in eleven sizes
portraits ageing in sequence, then stopping
something kept so well it has forgotten how to end
anchor: a vessel, sealed, still faintly warm
an hourglass that has never been turned
a casket sized for something smaller than a body

display.dangerLine: the barrow measures you against its host

institution: plinths along the stair, each holding a rival's finest thing
a gallery of gifts, none of them opened
cases arranged so the best is always further in
ritual: trophies mounted at a height that forces you to look up
a book recording who admired what, and for how long
a ribbon for every visitor who conceded the point
demand: an empty plinth, larger than the rest, waiting
a room that leaves you nowhere to stand but the centre
a case angled so you see yourself beside the prize
wound: a case of crowns, each slightly better than the last, all of them scratched
gifts defaced by whoever gave them
a plinth toppled, and the label kept
anchor: the piece every rival was meant to want, still under glass
a case holding one item and a great deal of space
a lock polished more often than the thing it guards

company.dangerLine: the barrow does not like it when people leave

institution: two sets of footprints in the dust, going in only
bedding laid for more than were ever buried
a coat-rack, full
ritual: chairs drawn up in a circle, all facing one seat
places set every evening for three hundred years
a table laid for more than were ever buried here
demand: hands, skeletal, holding other hands, the length of a hall
a doorway with the hinges taken off
a room arranged for a conversation that never ended
wound: a door barred from the inside, and the marks of it
scratches on the inside of a lid
a name called so often it wore into the wall
anchor: a keepsake still warm from being held
a chair kept empty and dusted
a second cup, always out

confession.dangerLine: the barrow is still listening for the right answer

institution: a kneeler worn through to the stone
a screen with a hole cut at the height of a mouth
benches facing one small window
ritual: written confessions, thousands, all in the same hand
a bell rung to begin, still roped
a queue of the dead facing a curtain
demand: a chamber where the echo answers differently than you spoke
a scale with a feather on one side and nothing on the other
a seat that will not let you rise until you have spoken
wound: a page torn from every book at the same place
a mouth chiselled off a statue
absolutions burned, and the ash kept
anchor: a confession nobody ever heard, sealed
a ledger of sins with the last page blank
a box that has only ever been opened once

precedence.dangerLine: the barrow keeps its order, and you have joined the queue

institution: a stair too grand for the door it serves
the dead laid in strict order of rank, heads toward the centre
numbered flagstones, counting down
ritual: banners in sequence, each house a place further back
a herald's script with the order still marked
a queue that has not moved
demand: a corridor that will not let two walk abreast
a door only one person may pass at a time, and only first
a threshold worn on one side only
wound: rank-plates prised off and swapped
a name moved to the front by force, repeatedly
a procession that doubled back on itself
anchor: the crown worn first, and only once
a staff of precedence, laid down
a seat at the head of everything, occupied

factions.name: the Barrow-Wardens
factions.essence: sealed this place and stayed to make sure

factions.name: things that moved in
factions.essence: neither know nor care whose tomb this is

features: a door that has been wedged open from the inside
a hole broken through a wall, recently, and not by you
water that has got in and taken three centuries to do it
a lamp still burning on oil that should be long gone
a collapse that has opened a way the builders never meant
a floor mosaic worn only along one path
an alcove emptied in a hurry

decisions.cue: two ways on: one narrow and dark, one wide and announced
decisions.cost: the wide way is faster and the barrow hears it

decisions.cue: a sealed door, and a crack you could squeeze through
decisions.cost: the crack costs skin and a Bane on a failure
carrying it slows you and it is not yours

decisions.cue: a member of the faction, alone and not yet hostile
decisions.cost: talking costs time; not talking costs later
everything gets wet, including what burns
leaving now means it will be worse when you return

temptations.cue: a courtier's mask, gold leaf over lime-wood, the mouth fixed in a small smile

temptations.standingDrawback: while worn you cannot be recognised by name

temptations.benefit: doors that answer to rank open for you
temptations.standingDrawback: the barrow's servants bring you their problems

temptations.cue: a hand-mirror that shows the room a moment behind
temptations.benefit: once per scene, see what was just here
temptations.standingDrawback: your reflection lags, and others notice

temptations.cue: a book of names, one line left blank
temptations.benefit: write a name and the Host obeys it once
temptations.standingDrawback: your own name is now in it

temptations.cue: a small crown, sized for someone who never grew
temptations.benefit: +1 die when others must defer to you
temptations.standingDrawback: you must be addressed correctly or lose the benefit

seal.function: the only thing the household answers to

vessel.label: a sealed jar holding one good year

ornament.label: the piece every rival was meant to want

token.label: a keepsake they would not be parted from
token.function: the promise that someone would stay

testament.label: a confession nobody ever heard
testament.function: the only account of what was done

regalia.label: the crown worn first, and only once

skirmish.avoid: they do not open hostilities on a guest

foes.name: Ghoul
foes.note: on a hit, a free Called Shot to freeze for a round

fight.avoid: the Ghoul goes for court dress first — send someone plain

triggerGlossary.seenTwice: reflected, echoed or witnessed twice over in one place

triggerGlossary.lingering: stayed in one place longer than it takes to search it
